whenAndWhere: Leipziger Strasse, Mitte, April 2005: a wide road between the Wall's old line and the new towers at Potsdamer Platz, empty lots still on both sides, in a city that has run out of money.
inTheAir: The Senate is in court claiming a budget emergency the federal government must fix, and selling city land while it argues.
Hartz IV came into force in January and a large part of the room is now living under it.
The Palast der Republik stands stripped and full of temporary art with the demolition order waiting, so nobody here believes that use protects a building.
The Wertheim heirs' restitution claim over this ground has run for years and the sale went through regardless.
Cheap flights into Schoenefeld have started bringing weekend crowds who arrive knowing the name and nothing else.
contested: Some say the weekend visitors are what keeps the city's clubs open at all; others answer that they are why the rent under them moved.
Some say a room ending is ordinary in a city that has always run on temporary use; others answer that temporary use was a story told by people who owned nothing.
exhausted: Rusted steel and safe-door photography, used by every cellar in the city.
Ostalgie: Trabants, Ampelmaennchen, the crest, finished since the film two years ago.
The anniversary number in a circle, which is the thing this is not.
The fisheye crowd with hands up over a footer of mobile-network logos.

whoIsWatching.audience: A man of thirty-one is leaving another club at four in the morning when something is put in his hand, and he is drunk enough to read one line of it. He has lived here since the mid-nineties and assumes everything closes eventually. A specific street number would hold him; being told what a legend the place was would not.
whoIsWatching.adversary: The new owner's site manager, who has an insurance date for handover and will call the district office about noise and about anything announcing an event after the building is surrendered.

transplants.ref: Roman evocatio, the calling-out of a besieged city's gods before its destruction
transplants.why: It ends a place formally by addressing what lived in it, rather than mourning the walls.

transplants.ref: The American wake, held in nineteenth-century Ireland for emigrants who would not return
transplants.why: A gathering that treats a departure as a death and lets people say so out loud.

transplants.ref: Shikinen sengu, the twenty-year dismantling and rebuilding of Ise Jingu
transplants.why: The ending is scheduled and attended, and the old timbers are kept and used elsewhere.

stakesLevelWhy: A room is being taken away and will not come back, which is a real loss on a fixed night, but nobody is harmed and nobody is at risk for turning up.
